method: Complete candidate survey followed by individual editorial choices and written reasons, applied to the existing complete guide to keep it within 300 quotations. All verified authorized selections included. Priority given to foundational teachings, substantive explanations, necessary qualifications, distinctive applications, narrative examples and thematic breadth across refuge and responsibility, protection from self, mercy toward those who cause harm, people in danger and the work of shelter, the cry of the oppressed, the Manifestation’s suffering, courage and a steadier heart, healing and care, children and families, women’s steadfastness, the Covenant and discernment, protective prayers and recitations, remembrance and gratitude, personal letters, wisdom and travel, and service. Neither citation count nor source order used as a ranking rule. The existing reading arc is retained.

selected.text: Through God have I remained vigilant in all matters, before all matters, and after all matters. Glory be unto Thee, O my God! Protect me from before me and behind me, from my right hand and my left, from above my head and beneath my feet, by virtue of that whereby Thou hast upheld the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them, and that which Thou hast bestowed upon me through Thy mercy and bounty. Verily, Thou art the Best of protectors
selected.reason: The Báb’s prayer in the Kitáb-i-Jazá’ for protection from before and behind, right and left, above and beneath, through the power that upholds the heavens; the encompassing form of protective prayer.

selected.text: Therefore unto Thee do I entrust the Tree of Thy oneness in me, with me, upon me, before me, after me, above me, beneath me, before my face, and from every direction. However Thou dost cause it to flourish, that is best for it; however Thou dost make it firm, that is glory for it; however Thou dost raise it up, that is a bounty for it from Thy presence.
selected.reason: The Báb’s entrusting of the Tree of oneness within Him to God from every direction, accepting however God makes it flourish; protection as surrender.

selected.text: O my Lord! selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer in the visitation tablet for Maryam, by her and the Manifestations of His names, not to be left to self and desires; a woman remembered in prayer.

selected.text: I beseech Thee, O my God, my Lord, my Creator and my Beloved, by the ocean of Thy Most Great Name, and by the heaven which Thou, O Lord of Eternity, hast raised up, to deliver Thy loved ones from those who have been so intoxicated with the wine of self-conceit that they have cast Thy Book behind their backs and followed Satan in whatsoever he commandeth them.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer that the loved ones be delivered from those intoxicated with the wine of self-conceit who cast His Book behind them; memorable image of pride.

Expand their breasts through the signs of Thy victory, attract their hearts through the breezes of Thy garden of grace, heal their ailments with the cup of Thy remedy, bind their wounds with the balm of Thy bounty and loving-kindness, strengthen their loins for Thy service, fortify their backs for Thy worship, and ordain for them guidance in their affairs.

selected.reason: The Báb’s prayer in a prison amulet text that the bearer of the green leaf be protected from every evil and brought into every good; historical protective form.

selected.text: O handmaidens of the All-Merciful! Raise your hands in supplication to the court of the Self-Sufficient Lord, saying: "O peerless Lord! Thou art holy and sanctified. Thou art compassionate and kind. Thou art the Succourer and the Helper. Verily, Thou art the Preserver, the Almighty, the Powerful, the All-Potent
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s call to the handmaidens to raise their hands and pray that the helpless be sheltered from the people of hypocrisy; a prayer given to women to say.

selected.text: My God, my God! Thou seest Thy loved ones beneath the talons of Thine enemies and hearest their cries and lamentations in Thy days. I beseech Thee by Thy loved ones whom the oppressors have torn limb from limb in the land of Ya, and by their blood and dismembered parts, to protect Thy loved ones through Thy power and deliver them from the wickedness of Thy creation.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer invoking loved ones torn limb from limb in Yazd, asking protection for the rest; keeps particular victims and their suffering visible.

selected.text: O Lord! O Forgiver! I am a weak servant and a frail being. You are the exalted refuge of the helpless and the strong sanctuary of the wanderers. The winds of trials are fierce and the tempests of tests uproot those near and far, and demolish the foundations of all, whether close or distant. Grant Your aid and protection, and withhold not Your pardon and forgiveness.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s confession of weakness before fierce winds of trial that uproot near and far, asking aid and pardon; fidelity amid tests.

selected.text: O my God and the God of all that are in the heavens and on earth! I beseech Thee by the Name through which the eyes were illumined, that Thou protect me from every affliction and hurt, and aid me to stand firm in this Cause whereby all who are on earth were shaken except such as were preserved through Thy Name, the All-Compelling, the Almighty, the All-Powerful.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer for protection from affliction and for firmness in a Cause by which all on earth were shaken save those preserved by the Name; steadiness in upheaval.

selected.text: O Lord! Thou seest them drawn to Thee, speaking Thy praise, bearing every hardship in Thy path, patient under Thy trials, persecuted by Thy servants. … O Lord! Prepare for them a way of right guidance, make them brilliant lamps unto all, stars rising in the midst of heaven, piercing meteors against those who would steal a hearing from among the weak Covenant-breakers
selected.reason: Prayer of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá for believers patient under persecution, that they become brilliant lamps and stars against Covenant-breakers; fidelity turned to radiance.

selected.text: I beseech Thee by the heaven and its stars and its radiance, and the moon and its light, and the earth and its waters and its bounties and its trees and what is treasured therein, and the seas and their pearls concealed within their shells, and by that which is within Thy knowledge and the treasuries of Thy power, to protect Thy loved ones from the evil of Thine enemies.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s invocation of the heaven and its stars, the moon, the earth and its waters and the seas with their hidden pearls, asking protection for the loved ones; memorable cosmic imagery.

selected.text: And recite at noon every day: "Glory be to God! There is no God but Him! And praise be to God Who hath not taken unto Himself a spouse nor a son, and Who hath no partner in sovereignty, nor any protector out of weakness. And magnify Him with all magnificence!" Then recite the Surih of Unity twelve times, and after each time say twice "God, my Lord, sufficeth all things."
selected.reason: The Báb’s instruction for Mullá Ḥasan to recite at noon a doxology and the Súrih of Unity twelve times with “God, my Lord, sufficeth all things”; a concrete recitation form.

selected.text: My God, my God, my Lord, my Support, my Master, my Helper, my Goal and my Object of worship! I beseech Thee by the lamp of Thy Cause which Thou didst kindle with the hand of Thy power, and by the pearls which were hidden in the hearts of Thy chosen ones, and by the ocean of Thy verses and the heaven of Thy generosity, to protect Thy friends through Thy bounty and Thy hosts.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer by the lamp of the Cause and the pearls hidden in the hearts of the chosen ones that His friends be protected; memorable devotional imagery.

selected.text: O my God, my Lord, and my Hope! I beseech Thee by the sovereignty of Thy power and the dominion of Thy might to protect Thy people from the whisperings of the devils and the promptings of the corrupters, and to guard the pearls of their love for Thee from the hands of the thieves. Verily, Thou art the Sovereign of all worlds and the Lord of the heavens
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer that the people be protected from devilish whisperings and that the pearls of their love be guarded from thieves; memorable image of inward treasure.

selected.text: O my Lord! Thou seest me and Thy loved ones in the hands of the oppressors among Thy creatures. I beseech Thee to transform their tyranny into justice and their oppression into equity. Then send down upon them from the heaven of Thy power that which will transform their fear into tranquility, their weakness into strength and might, and their agitation into supreme steadfastness.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer that the tyranny of oppressors be transformed into justice and the fear and weakness of His loved ones into tranquillity and strength; turns the opening toward justice.

selected.text: Make this land, O my God, blessed and secure for me. Guard me, then, O my God, at the time of my entering into it and my going out from it. Make it, then, a fortress for me and for whomsoever worships Thee and bows down before Thee, that I may be protected therein through Thy bounty and kept safe within it from the darts of those who have disbelieved in Thee, through Thy strength.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer that a land be made blessed and secure, guarding His entering and going out and making it a fortress for worshippers; protection in travel and dwelling.

selected.text: O Lord, Thou seest the believers among the idolaters, and what hath befallen them at the hands of the oppressors among Thy creation and the transgressors among Thy servants. I beseech Thee to preserve them through the hosts of Thy power and the legions of Thy might, then ordain for them what beseemeth the heaven of Thy generosity and the ocean of Thy mercy and the sun of Thy bounty
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer for believers living among idolaters and oppressors, that they be preserved by the hosts of divine power; the Manifestation’s care for His followers.

selected.text: O my Lord! I am Thy servant and the son of Thy servant. I testify to Thy unity and Thy singleness, and to the sanctity of Thy Being and the detachment of Thine Essence. O my Lord! Thou seest Thy trusted ones in the hands of the treacherous among Thy creatures and the slanderers among Thy creation, and Thou knowest what hath befallen us from those of whom Thou art more aware than we are.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s testimony to divine unity and lament that God’s trusted ones are in the hands of the treacherous and slanderers; the cry of the oppressed in His own voice.

selected.text: O Lord! Thou seest them turning away from the Known and advancing toward the imagined. O Lord! Deliver them through the arms of Thy power from the seas of idle fancies and vain imaginings, then grant them Thy sealed wine, whose seal was broken by Thy Self-Subsisting Name. O Lord! Withhold not Thy servants from the lights of Thy countenance, and deprive them not of the ocean of Thy bestowal.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer that those turning from the Known toward the imagined be delivered from seas of idle fancies and given the sealed wine; protection from illusion.

selected.text: O my Beloved! Thy most vehement enemies and antagonistic foes have assailed Thy helpless servant from every ambush where they lay in wait. They have descended upon me from every height, attacking like wolves and pouncing like dogs, fearing not the Day of Retribution. The clouds weep for Thy lowly servant, the doves lament, and the nightingales in the hearts of the loved ones cry out in anguish.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s lament that enemies attacked His helpless servant like wolves and dogs while clouds weep and doves lament; the Master’s own suffering in vivid imagery.

selected.text: O my God! Thou seest and knowest that the oppressors have wronged Thy loved ones who have turned toward the Dayspring of Thy Revelation, the Dawning-Place of Thine inspiration and the Source of Thy Cause, and have driven them, together with their children and their women, from their homeland - though they had manifested naught except that which Thou didst command them through Thy Most Exalted Pen.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s witness that oppressors drove the loved ones, with their women and children, from their homeland though they did only what God commanded; a precise account of displacement.

selected.text: O Lord of Names and Creator of Heaven! I beseech Thee by the Dawning-Place of Thy most excellent names and the Source of Thy most exalted attributes, Who has been imprisoned in Thy path amidst the wicked, that Thou aid me to make mention of Thee and praise Thee, and assist me in serving Thee in such wise that neither the might of the transgressors nor the power of the evil ones shall hold me back.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer, invoking the One imprisoned in God’s path, for help to praise and serve so that no power of transgressors may hold one back; joins protection to service.

selected.text: My God, my God! Praise be to Thee for having guided me to Thy most exalted horizon and for having caused me to recognize the Dawning-Place of Thy mighty signs. I beseech Thee by the Manifestations of Thy Revelation and the Daysprings of Thy inspiration to protect me from the evil of Thine enemies who have disbelieved in Thee and in Thy signs and have denied that which hath appeared from Thy presence.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s thanks for having been guided to recognize the Dawning-Place of His signs, with a plea for protection from those who deny it; recognition as the ground of firmness.

selected.text: My God, my God! Thou seest how the faithful are in the clutches of the faithless, and the near ones in the grasp of the transgressors. That which hath befallen them in Thy path hath not befallen any among Thy servants. Their hearts have melted in their separation from Thee, their tears have flowed in their remoteness from Thee, and their breasts are constricted by what hath come upon Thee in Thy days.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s lament that the faithful are in the clutches of the faithless, their hearts melted and tears flowing; the cry of the oppressed in His voice.

selected.text: Glory be to Thee, O Lord of the Kingdom and Sovereign of the realms of might! I beseech Thee by Thy Name through which the mountain would take flight were it to be cast upon it, through which the heavens would be cleft asunder, and through which the earth would be rent asunder, to protect us from the arrows of the insinuations of them that mislead and from the swords of the doubts of the idolaters.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer by the Name that would make a mountain take flight to protect us from the arrows of insinuation and swords of doubt; vivid image of divine power.

selected.text: O Lord of creation and Ruler over all lands! I beseech Thee by the Name through which was raised the shrill voice of Thy Most Exalted Pen between earth and heaven, to ordain for Thy chosen ones that which will bring tranquility to their souls and gladness to their hearts
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer by the shrill voice of the Most Exalted Pen that the chosen ones be granted tranquillity of soul and gladness of heart; assurance as divine gift.

selected.text: "O Lord! Free these sincere friends from tests and make these worthy servants successful through Your grace. Make each one a firm mountain and an unshakeable peak. Place the crown of servitude upon their heads and grant them eternal sovereignty. Bestow abundance in their livelihood and confer everlasting glory. You are the Giver, the Bestower, the Kind, and You are the Forgiver, the Acceptor, the Mighty, the Helper."
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s prayer that sincere friends be freed from tests, made firm mountains and unshakeable peaks, crowned with servitude and granted livelihood; protection, character and provision together.

selected.text: I beseech Thee by Thy radiant and effulgent light, and by Thy mighty and wondrous Name, whereby the realities of names were shaken and the manifestations of wickedness and indecency lamented, to adorn the temples of Thy servants with the raiment of godliness and their heads with the crown of steadfastness and detachment, that they may not be frightened by the might of the oppressors nor the tyranny of the aggressors.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer that the servants be clothed in godliness and crowned with steadfastness and detachment so that oppressors cannot frighten them; courage as inward adornment.

selected.text: My God, my God! Thou seest the Wronged One making mention of Thy loved ones and acquainting them with that which draweth them nigh unto the court of Thy glory. I beseech Thee by the ocean of Thy power and the heaven of Thy bounty to aid them to be steadfast in Thy love and to illumine their hearts with the lights of Thy knowledge. Then protect them from the evil of Thine enemies who have disbelieved in Thee and Thy signs
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer, as the Wronged One who mentions His loved ones, that they be steadfast in love and illumined with knowledge; care conveyed through correspondence.

selected.text: When thou hearest the cooing of the Dove of My utterance upon the branches of the Tree of My knowledge, say: "My God, my God! I testify to Thy oneness and Thy singleness, and that Thou hast no partner in Thy dominion nor any equal in Thy kingdom. I beseech Thee by the waves of the ocean of Thy power and the effulgences of the lights of the Sun of Thy oneness to protect me from the evil of Thine enemies and to draw me nigh unto Thee
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer, to be said on hearing the Dove of His utterance, testifying to God’s oneness and asking protection from enemies and nearness; a prayer given for use.

selected.text: O Lord! I beseech Thee by Thy Name through which Thou hast subdued all who are in the heavens and earth, through which Thy remembrance was exalted, Thy proof was established, Thy evidences appeared, and Thy verses were sent down, to assist Thy loved ones in that which Thou hast purposed for them through Thy bounty and favor. Then deliver them from the fire of self and passion, and cause them to enter beneath the shadow of Thy Most Great Mercy.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer that the loved ones be assisted in God’s purpose and delivered from the fire of self and passion; inward protection in the closing movement.

selected.text: O God! O Thou Who dost strengthen the sincere ones with hosts from the Most Glorious Kingdom and Who dost confirm those firm in Thy Covenant with legions of angels from the Supreme Concourse! This servant, submissive and humble before Thy exalted Threshold, calls upon Thee, supplicating and imploring before Thy Most Great Mercy, taking refuge in the cave of Thy protection and most mighty safekeeping, that Thou wouldst protect him from the evil of enemies
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s prayer to the One Who strengthens the sincere with hosts and angels, as a humble servant taking refuge in the cave of protection; refuge from enemies.

selected.text: Glory be to Thee, O my God! Thou verily knowest my abasement and poverty, and seest my burning anguish and distress, and hearest my moaning and lamenting and my cry of grief. … I beseech Thy exalted threshold and Thy most sublime sanctuary, and in utter lowliness and contrition I turn to the Kingdom of Mysteries and pray on behalf of the righteous, that they may be enabled to serve among the free and find refuge in the cave of Thy protection from the wicked
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s prayer from burning anguish on behalf of the righteous, that they serve among the free and find refuge from the wicked; suffering turned to intercession.

selected.text: O my Lord! I am Thy servant and the son of Thy servant. I have turned unto Thee with the turning of one who is assured, seeing, confident and informed. I beseech Thee by Thy Name whereby Thou hast illumined the world to set right my affairs and to ordain for me from the Pen of Thy decree that which will bring me into Thy presence. Then decree for me, O my God, that which will preserve me from the clamor of the heedless ones and the uproar of the treacherous ones.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer, turning with assurance, that God set right His affairs and preserve Him from the clamor of the heedless; practical affairs within prayer.

selected.text: O Lord, O Possessor of forgiveness, pardon and beneficence! This servant is related to one who was embraced by the glances of Thy merciful eyes in the world of lights. He cries unto Thee for deliverance from the evil of the wicked, and seeks refuge in the shelter of Thy mercy, the gathering-place of hopes. … He seeks assistance through Thy might and power, O Possessor of firm strength and dominion triumphant over all the worlds. Verily Thou art the Deliverer of those in distress
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s prayer for one related to a soul embraced by divine mercy, crying for deliverance and seeking the Deliverer of those in distress; kinship and intercession.

selected.text: O my God! I complain unto Thee of the manifestation of wickedness and rebellion and corruption, and that which hath come between Thee and Thy servants. I beseech Thee by Thy Name, O Lord of the Day of Mutual Calling, to protect us through Thy sovereignty and power and to make us of those who soar in Thine atmosphere. Then gather us beneath the shade of the shelter of Thy mercy in every world of Thy worlds. Verily Thou art the Almighty, the All-Glorious, the Help in Peril.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s complaint of wickedness and corruption coming between God and His servants, asking to be gathered beneath the shelter of mercy in every world; the Help in Peril.

selected.text: I am the one who is in misery, O God! Behold me cleaving fast to Thy Name, the All-Possessing. I am the one who is sure to perish; behold me clinging to Thy Name, the Imperishable. I implore Thee, therefore, by Thy Self, the Exalted, the Most High, not to abandon me unto mine own self and unto the desires of a corrupt inclination. Hold Thou my hand with the hand of Thy power, and deliver me from the depths of my fancies and idle imaginings, and cleanse me of all that is abhorrent unto Thee.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: My God, my God! I am he who hath turned unto Thee and believed in Thee and in Thy signs. I beseech Thee by the Standard of Thy Cause which neither the tempestuous winds can move nor the succession of centuries and ages can change, to make me in all conditions to hold fast unto Thee, to take refuge in Thy Presence, to seek protection with Thy Self, and to abide beneath Thy shadow. Verily, Thou art the Omnipotent over whatsoever Thou willest. There is none other God but Thee, the Forgiving, the Generous.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer, by the Standard that neither tempests nor centuries can move, to hold fast to God and abide beneath His shadow in all conditions; a memorable statement of constancy.

selected.text: O God! Assist them through the power of Thy celestial might and enable them through the force of Thy divine dominion. Open before their faces the doors of triumph and grant them sustenance from the table of heaven, O Thou Most Holy and Most Glorious! Make for them a way out and ordain for them provision, and sustain them from Thy hidden treasuries. Make them victorious over those who have harmed them and protect them in the shelter of Thy protection through Thy aid and bounty, Thy safeguarding and preservation
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s prayer that the persecuted be given a way out, provision from hidden treasuries and victory over those who harmed them; practical and spiritual aid together.

selected.text: O my God, my God! These are Thy chosen, pure, mindful and faithful servants among all humanity. They have been afflicted by the ignorant ones. Thy gazelles in the wilderness of unity and faithfulness have fallen under the fangs of dogs and wolves, and Thy sheep have been caught in the claws of hungry beasts. O Lord! Guard them through Thy protection, the eye of Thy care and Thy shelter from the evil of the wicked, base, ignoble enemies. Verily Thou art the Strong, the Mighty, the Powerful, the Protector, the Wise.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s lament that God’s gazelles have fallen under the fangs of dogs and wolves and His sheep into the claws of hungry beasts; vivid image of persecuted faithfulness.

selected.text: My God, my God! Thou seest me weakened by fasting and standing in prayer, and my strength has waned in the darkness of these nights. I am unable to count the praises of Thy Most Glorious Beauty, and I bow my face to the dust in humility before Thy greatness and might, which has appeared like the sun at high noon on the Day of Return. I beseech Thee to assist Thy owned servant Baqir, revealer of mysteries and vanquisher of the wicked, and to strengthen him with mighty hosts of grace and benevolence in every time and place.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s prayer, weakened by fasting and night prayer, asking that a servant be strengthened with hosts of grace in every time and place; intercession from personal exhaustion.

selected.text: Glorified art Thou, O Lord my God! O Thou Who art my God, and my Master, and my Lord, and my Support, and my Hope, and my Refuge, and my Light. I ask of Thee, by Thy Hidden and Treasured Name, which none knoweth save Thine own Self, to protect the bearer of this Tablet from every calamity and pestilence, and from every wicked man and woman; from the evil of the evil-doers, and from the scheming of the unbelievers. Preserve him, moreover, O my God, from every pain and vexation, O Thou Who holdest in Thy hand the empire of all things.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: I beseech Thee by Thy Name through which Thou didst bring the contingent beings into existence and didst manifest all created things, and through which Thou didst rend asunder the veils from the face of all who are in the heavens and on earth, that Thou mayest cause this poor one and these poor ones who have emigrated with him to enter the city of Thy riches within the pavilion of Thy glory and might. Then assist us with the wonders of Thy help, clothe us in the garment of Thy love, and deprive us not, O my God, of what lieth with Thee
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer that the poor one and those who emigrated with him enter the city of divine riches and be clothed in love; exile and companionship.

selected.text: O my Lord! Protect me from those on whose faces is seen the dust of hell-fire. Then aid me in Thy remembrance and praise, and make me steadfast in such wise that neither the veils of the peoples of creation nor the whisperings of the evil ones shall prevent me. O my Lord! Thou hast guided me to the Dayspring of Thy Cause and the Dawning-Place of Thy inspiration. I beseech Thee by Thy Most Great Name, whereby Thou hast distinguished between the nations, to protect me beneath the pavilion of Thy mercy and the tabernacle of Thy glory. Verily, Thou art the Almighty, the Forgiving, the Merciful.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer for protection from those whose faces bear the dust of hell-fire and for steadfastness that no veils or whisperings can prevent; remembrance and firmness.

selected.text: O Lord! When Thou didst rend their garments in Thy love, and burn their hearts with the flames of longing ignited by Thy remembrance, and remove their restraint in their passion for Thee, and make them renowned through Thy name among Thy servants, and exalt their names in Thy Books and Scriptures - preserve them from the evil of Thine enemies among Thy creation, and guard them with the eye of Thy protection and care, and shield them from the arrows of the oppressors' tyranny, and protect them from the spears of the treacherous ones' betrayal, and keep them within the sanctuary of Thy help and protection
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s prayer for lovers whose garments were rent and hearts burned in longing, that they be shielded from tyranny and betrayal; devotion and protection joined.

selected.text: My God, my God! Thou hearest the cry of the sincere ones, the lament of them that are nigh unto Thee, and the sighing of them that know Thee, when Thine enemies have encompassed them from every direction and there hath befallen them that which hath caused the dwellers of the cities of names to wail. I beseech Thee, O my God, by them and by those who have offered up their lives in Thy path and have expended all they possessed in their longing to meet Thee, to assist Thy loved ones with the hosts of the unseen and of the visible realm. Then protect them from the evil of every oppressive enemy and every wicked transgressor.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer, by the martyrs who gave their lives, that loved ones encompassed by enemies be assisted with the hosts of the seen and unseen; the cry of the sincere.

selected.text: Glory be unto Thee, O God of Names, Creator of the heavens, Who hath appeared before the faces of enemies and speaketh from the supreme horizon! Thou seest Thy loved ones in the hands of the oppressors, and in every moment there befalleth them that which causeth faces to change and beings to be set ablaze. I beseech Thee, O Source of Bounty, by Thy Name through which Thou made the sweet waters of Thy mercy to flow among Thy servants, and by Thy Command whereby the trumpet was blown and they that lay in their graves arose, to aid Thy loved ones to remember and praise Thee, and to protect them from the evil of Thy creatures.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer, as One appearing before His enemies, that loved ones afflicted at every moment be aided to remember and praise God and protected; the Manifestation’s voice in danger.

selected.text: O my God!
